name: X2: end-to-end catalogue test with Muse (one can product, S19) on the Three.js engine
description: Last task. Proves the merged branch end to end on ONE catalogue product (a can): runs the paid S19 catalogue live script with Muse under a hard budget on a one-product feed, converts and plays the produced film on the Three.js player in headless Chromium, opens it in the studio, and writes a report with cost, screenshots and results. The S20 cinematic run and the cartoon (toon) story are out of scope.

userStories.title: Budget check: estimate S19 on a one-can feed without spending
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want the cost known before any paid call so that the test stays under budget.
steps: Check which keys the S19 live script needs against .env.example and whether they are set (print only 'set' or 'missing', never the value).

Create fixtures/catalog/feed-1.csv with the header of fixtures/catalog/feed-6.csv and exactly one product that is a can (drinks category) taken from feed-6.csv. Run npm run live -- s19-catalog fixtures/catalog/feed-1.csv (no --yes) and record the printed estimate.
Start docs/e2e-catalog-report.md with the keys status, the estimate and the budget cap of 2 dollars.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/e2e-catalog-report.md has the estimate and the keys status, and the estimate is under 2 dollars (or the story records why the run is skipped)
fixtures/catalog/feed-1.csv has exactly one product row and parses with parseFeed from shared/catalog
No API key value appears in docs/e2e-catalog-report.md or debug/ralph logs (grep for 'sk-' and 'Bearer' prints nothing)

userStories.title: Run S19 live with Muse on the one-can feed
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want the catalogue path to produce real films so that the demo is proven.
steps: Run npm run live -- s19-catalog fixtures/catalog/feed-1.csv --yes once and keep its output in debug/app/e2e/s19.log.
List the films and index written under web/public/cartoon/catalog/ for the can and record the actual cost printed by the run in the report.
acceptanceCriteria: web/public/cartoon/catalog/ has an index and at least one film per product
The report lists the produced film files and the real cost

userStories.title: The produced can film converts and plays on the Three.js engine
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want each produced film to play on the new engine so that Three.js carries the demo.
steps: Write e2e/catalog-motion.spec.ts (or a node script with vitest if simpler): for the film from US-002, parse with parseAepCompositionSafe, convert with aepToMotion from web/src/motion/aep (zero 'skipped' warnings for supported kinds), then open the dev page http://localhost:5173/aep-motion.html with that film in headless Chromium, take screenshots at 25 % and 75 % into debug/app/e2e/, and check the page has no console errors, the canvas is not blank and the two frames differ.
Run it and record per-film results (warnings count, screenshots) in the report.
acceptanceCriteria: Every produced film parses, converts and renders non-blank frames that differ between 25 % and 75 %, or the report lists the exact film and reason it did not

Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`

userStories.title: Studio check: open the produced can film in the studio on the motion engine
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want the studio to play a catalogue film so that the whole app path works.
steps: Find how a produced catalogue film opens in the studio (gallery or the catalogue studio page, see web/src/ and docs of S15 if present after the merge). Use headless Chromium on http://localhost:5173 to open the S19 can film, press play, seek to the middle, and save screenshots to debug/app/e2e/.
Record console errors (none expected) and the film ids in the report.
acceptanceCriteria: One studio screenshot show the film drawn by the motion engine, or the report names the blocker
The console has no errors during play and seek

Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`
userStories.notes: Browser check (engine playwright on :5290, API mocked): /?film=cb-original shows 3D can, $4.50 price, accent disc on dark plate; Play advanced to 0:02.0, seek to 0:02.5, no console errors. Screenshot debug/engine/studio-cb-original.png.

userStories.title: Final report and full gate
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want one report so that I can see what was proven and what remains.
steps: Complete docs/e2e-catalog-report.md: what ran, total live spend against the 2 dollar cap, pass or fail per film, screenshots list, remaining warning kinds with counts, and open problems.
Run npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test and record the results.
acceptanceCriteria: The report states the total live spend (under 2 dollars) and a pass or fail for every film
npm run typecheck and npm run lint pass and npm test is green

readFirst: scripts/live/s19-catalog.ts (header says what it does and costs) and scripts/live/run.ts
.env.example (which keys the live scripts need; never print .env)
web/src/dev/aep-motion.tsx (dev page that plays a stored film on the engine)
metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; use the stored films under data/films/*/versions/*.json (read with node:fs) and assets under web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md and engine/docs/README.md before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.
The app's composition format is AepCompositionJson from `@shared/aep` (our own copy of the schema). Never import `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `pixi.js`, `@pixi/*` or `pixi-filters` in new code.

Use the engine through `@engine/*` (engine/src). Do not edit engine/ except the files in metadata.sharedEdits; if the engine lacks something, add a row to docs/todos/ENGINE-NEEDS.md, use a workaround and say so in notes.
Edit only the files the story names, their tests, and metadata.sharedEdits. Do not change server/ behaviour, agent prompts or stored films.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore`. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/app/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (already running; do not start another); headless Chromium through @playwright/test is fine.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.

`npm test` has 11 known failures outside your files (10 in scripts/preflight/docs.test.ts, 1 in web/src/authoring-agreement.test.tsx). Do not edit those files. The `npm test` gate passes when no other test fails.

The dev server on http://localhost:5173 is owner-run and shared: never kill, restart or stop it (no kill/pkill/lsof-kill on vite or port 5173). If it is down, use headless Chromium against `npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts --port 5180 --strictPort` started and stopped by you, and only that one.

EXCEPTION to the offline rule above, for this PRD only: the live scripts may call the paid services they are written for (SAM, Muse). HARD BUDGET: total live spend for the whole PRD must stay under 2 US dollars (one product, one can). Test ONLY the S19 catalogue path on ONE can product. Do not run s20-cinematic, the cartoon or toon scripts, or any other live script. Always run a live script first WITHOUT --yes to read its printed estimate; if the estimate is above 1.5 dollars, stop and record it. Run each live script with --yes at most once; never loop or retry a paid call; if a paid run fails, record the error and stop spending. Keep a running spend tally in docs/e2e-catalog-report.md.
Never print, log or commit API keys or .env. If a key is missing, record which one in notes, skip the paid step and mark the story's acceptance as not met (do not fake a result).
Browser checks use the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (already running; never kill it) and headless Chromium through @playwright/test.
